## Cross-repository visual consistency and legacy-language policy

- Treat every supplied or regenerated image as reference intake until canon, originality, anatomy, gameplay, and production review is recorded. Never silently promote an image, name, form, or costume into the 125-ID Permanent Eco-Kin Dex.
- Whole-game visual target: polished proprietary **Anime-toon** rendering with consistent character identity, silhouette, face, anatomy, scale, markings, costume, palette, and established Eco-Kin evolution lineage across scenes, UI, cinematics, marketing, and Unreal assets.
- Preserve approved reference identity. Do not arbitrarily change faces, species, body type, hairstyle, skin tone, clothing, signature equipment, names, or established forms. Intentional Mutation, Shimmer Form, damage, age, or costume changes must be labeled and cross-referenced.
- For regenerated art, use dark teal/indigo environmental structure, cyan resonance light, and restrained amber highlights when compatible with the source. Preserve the original composition unless a requested production format requires a documented crop or layout change.
- Replace ordinary real-world weapons with clearly fictional A.E.G.I.S.-linked resonance tools when adapting concepts for production. Maintain safe, readable anatomy and avoid copied franchise, celebrity, religious, mythological, or protected design language.
- In-image text must use exact approved spelling. Run a text, name, anatomy, hand/limb, equipment, and continuity QA pass before accepting art. If exact typography cannot be guaranteed, deliver clean art without text and add typography in an editable design layer.
- COBOL and BASIC may be used only in isolated, optional legacy utilities: deterministic data conversion, validation fixtures, import/export bridges, diagnostic reports, or reproducible experiments. Pin the exact dialect/compiler and version, include build/run instructions and tests, keep inputs/outputs schema-versioned, and sandbox untrusted files.
- Never use COBOL or BASIC to replace Unreal Engine 5.8 C++/Blueprint gameplay, replication, animation, UI, save, packaging, dedicated-server, platform, or rendering responsibilities; never replace TypeScript/JavaScript web code or approved Python/PowerShell build tooling without a reviewed migration.
- Never claim COBOL/BASIC, art, Unreal, or cross-repository integration is compiled, rendered, imported, or VERIFIED without direct evidence from the applicable toolchain and runtime.
